pages.text: A program starts at the north end of a sheet and runs south. Each row of blocks across the sheet is a $(l)line$(). The first line is line 0.

Inside a sheet, x counts from the west edge. Language blocks go between x=5 and x=28, so a line holds at most 24 blocks. That keeps lines short and easy to read.$(br2)At x=4 there is a gray rail: the $(l)cursor rail$(). When a program runs, a glowing cursor moves along it and shows which line is working right now.
